sources.entry: TransporterPad - iOS/Android app deployment tool for macOS.

summary.one_liner: TransporterPad is a macOS app that installs .ipa (iOS) and .apk (Android) app packages onto USB-connected devices by dragging files into its window.
summary.what_it_does: The tool lets non-engineers such as designers or planners install app packages without setting up Xcode or the Android SDK. The user starts TranspoterPad.app and connects a device by USB, and the device appears in the window. Users drop an .ipa or .apk file, or a link to an app package such as a Jenkins artifact link dragged from Safari, into the window. Clicking the "Beam UP!" button uploads the app. If several devices are connected, the app is uploaded to all of them at once.
use_cases: install ipa files on an iPhone without Xcode
install apk files on an Android phone from a Mac
share test builds with non-engineer team members
install a Jenkins build artifact onto a device
deploy one app build to multiple connected devices
how_to_run: Connect the device to the Mac with USB
For iOS, authorize the connection in iTunes or Xcode
For Android, enable Developer Mode and Debug Interface on the device
Drop an .ipa or .apk file (or app package link) into the TransporterPad window
notable: Needs no Xcode or Android SDK installation for the user
Accepts dragged app package links, such as Jenkins artifact URLs
Uploads to all connected devices at once
Supports both iOS (.ipa) and Android (.apk) packages
caveats: iOS devices must be authorized for connection through iTunes or Xcode first
Android devices need Developer Mode and Debug Interface enabled
README does not describe build or install steps for developers
keywords: install app on device from mac
